title: Peanut Sauce

items.raw: ½ cup (130 g) creamy peanut butter
1 tablespoon honey or light brown sugar
1–2 teaspoons sriracha or chili garlic sauce

steps.text: Put the peanut butter, soy sauce, lime juice, rice vinegar, honey, sesame oil, garlic, ginger, and 1 teaspoon of sriracha in a bowl.
Add ⅓ cup of hot water and whisk. It will look broken and lumpy at first — keep whisking and it will come together smooth and glossy.
For dipping, stop when it is as thick as heavy cream. For tossing with noodles or dressing a salad, whisk in more hot water a tablespoon at a time until it pours easily.

Taste and adjust: more lime for brightness, more soy for salt, more honey for sweetness, more sriracha for heat. It should taste bold on its own, since it will be spread thin over whatever it dresses.
Serve at room temperature in a small bowl for dipping, or toss with cooked noodles, shredded cabbage, cucumber, and scallions.

notes.label: Natural peanut butter
notes.text: works, but stir the jar well first and expect a slightly thinner, less sweet sauce. Add an extra teaspoon of honey.

notes.label: Ahead of time
notes.text: keeps a week refrigerated. It thickens to a paste when cold; whisk in a little hot water to bring it back.

notes.label: Coconut version
notes.text: replace the water with warmed coconut milk and add a teaspoon of red curry paste for a richer satay-style sauce.

notes.label: Uses
notes.text: cold sesame noodles, chicken or tofu satay, fresh spring rolls, grilled vegetables, or a dressing for a crunchy cabbage salad.

openQuestion: This is a best guess — a Thai-style peanut sauce with lime, soy, and a little heat. Who makes it, and what does it go with in your family — noodles, summer rolls, satay, the Napa salad? Tell me if yours is made with coconut milk, and how spicy it should be.
